mainTopic: The סיינא hat on שבת, and the משניות on what the מקדש allows: hinge pins, bandages and harp strings
overview: This amud opens by finishing a rule about canopies: a slanted side of a טפח counts as a real אוהל. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי permits wearing a stiff felt hat (סיינא) on שבת. After one rejected answer, the גמרא concludes that a tight hat is allowed, while a loose one is forbidden because it might fall off and be carried. Next comes a series of משניות about things the מקדש allows on שבת that are forbidden elsewhere. First is putting back a door's hinge pin. A ברייתא explains why the upper pin is forbidden, and it adds that doors attached to the ground may never be fixed. The second משנה is about putting a bandage back on a wound. The ברייתא records a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה, followed by שמואל's ruling, רב חסדא's limit, and a story about רב אשי putting back a bandage that fell on a pillow. The last משנה allows tying a broken harp string in the מקדש. The גמרא resolves a contradiction from a ברייתא and ends by asking which view רבי יהודה follows; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A slope of one handbreadth counts as a tent
steps.stepSummary: The end of a qualification: a canopy is allowed only if its slope is less than a טפח, because a slope of a טפח or more counts as a real אוהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: …does not have a handbreadth in its slope. But if its slope does have a handbreadth, the slopes of tents are considered like tents.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts mid-sentence, finishing a rule from the previous lines about when a canopy may be put up on שבת. It adds that if the slanted side extends a טפח, it counts as a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier permission covered only a canopy with no flat roof of a טפח. This line adds that a slanted side of a טפח also counts, because a slope can act as a roof just like a flat top. So a canopy with a טפח of slope is forbidden to set up on שבת, since that would be making an אוהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Slope or incline; a slanted side
A handbreadth, the minimum size for a tent-roof
Tent; making one on Shabbat is forbidden
Are considered like, are compared to

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'בשיפועה טפח' complete a phrase from the previous lines, 'when there is not in its slope a טפח'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of 'one טפח makes a tent', which the גמרא will try to apply to the hat in step 4.

phrases.english: [when there is not] a handbreadth in its slope,
phrases.notes: Continues the sentence from the previous lines.

phrases.english: but if its slope does have a handbreadth —
the slopes of tents are considered like tents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל יֵשׁ בְּשִׁיפּוּעָהּ טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a qualification begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slanted side of a טפח or more makes the structure an אוהל, so setting it up is forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: A stiff felt hat is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי rules that one may wear a סיינא on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: a felt hat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: the same אמורא says that wearing a stiff felt hat on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This hat has a firm brim that sticks out, so it may look a little like a small tent over the head. Even so, רב שישא permits it. The next steps will test this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A stiff felt hat with a brim
Permitted

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
A felt hat — is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by the same speaker, still on the theme of tents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing a סיינא on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: A teaching says the hat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שישא from a ברייתא that forbids the felt hat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that a ברייתא says the exact opposite of רב שישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא should not argue with a ברייתא. So the גמרא needs to explain how both statements can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא
Forbidden

phrases.english: But it was taught: it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא's permission to wear a סיינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly forbids what he permits.

steps.title: First answer: it depends on whether the brim is a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids a hat whose brim sticks out a טפח, since that is like a tent. רב שישא permits one whose brim is less.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is where it has a handbreadth, and that one is where it does not have a handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources describe two different hats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer uses the rule from step 1, that a טפח of overhang makes a tent. A brim of a טפח would count as an אוהל and be forbidden. A smaller brim would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; both can be true
That has in it
That does not have in it

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this — where it has a handbreadth,
phrases.notes: This is the case the ברייתא forbids.

phrases.english: that — where it does not have a handbreadth.
phrases.notes: This is the case where רב שישא permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the two sources simply disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: They refer to different brim sizes, and the tent rule decides which is which.

steps.title: Then is pulling a cloak forward forbidden too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer: if a טפח of overhang makes a tent, then pulling a cloak a טפח past the head would also be forbidden, which is absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, if he extended his cloak a handbreadth, would that also be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer by showing where it would lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People pull a cloak forward over the head all the time, and nobody treats that as building a tent. Clothing worn on the body is not an אוהל. So the 'one טפח' reasoning cannot be the real reason for forbidding the hat.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, according to this reasoning
Extended, stuck out
Cloak
Is it really so as well?

phrases.english: But if so:
if he extended his cloak a handbreadth,
would it also be forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 4 leads to an absurd result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that a brim of a טפח makes the hat an אוהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By that logic, an ordinary cloak pulled forward would also be forbidden, and clearly it is not.

steps.title: Final answer: a tight hat is allowed, a loose hat is not
steps.stepSummary: The real difference is fit. A snug hat is permitted. A loose one is forbidden, because it may fall off and the wearer may carry it in the street.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this one is where it fits tightly, and that one is where it does not fit tightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the tent idea and gives a new way to settle the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is now carrying, not tents. רב שישא permits a hat that sits firmly on the head, since it will not fall. The ברייתא forbids a loose hat, because it might blow off and the person might carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Fits tightly, is pressed firmly on
Public domain, where carrying is forbidden on Shabbat

steps.whatToRemember: A סיינא may be worn on שבת only if it fits tightly. The worry is that a loose hat could fall off and be carried, not that the hat counts as a tent.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not hold onto the 'one טפח' answer from step 4. It was rejected, and the final reason has nothing to do with tents.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this — where it fits tightly,
phrases.notes: This is the case where רב שישא permits it.

phrases.english: that — where it does not fit tightly.
phrases.notes: This is the case the ברייתא forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 4 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases on a new basis (carrying instead of tents)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was thought to be brim size, because of the tent rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is how tightly the hat fits, because of the fear of carrying it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A tight felt hat is permitted. A loose one is forbidden because it might be carried in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The משנה: lower hinge pin allowed in the Temple, upper pin forbidden everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that the lower hinge pin may be put back in the מקדש but not in the מדינה, and the upper pin may not be put back anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may put back the lower hinge pin in the Temple, but not in the rest of the country. And the upper one is forbidden both here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on putting a slipped hinge pin back into place on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting back the lower pin is easy and only forbidden by the רבנן, and rabbinic decrees of this kind (שבות) do not apply in the מקדש. The upper pin is harder to put in and counts as real building, which is forbidden by the תורה. Torah laws apply even in the מקדש, so the upper pin is forbidden everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Hinge pin, the peg a door turns on
The Temple, where most rabbinic שבת decrees do not apply
The rest of the country, anywhere outside the Temple
An action forbidden on שבת by rabbinic decree only

steps.confusionAlert: "כאן וכאן" means "in the מקדש and in the מדינה," meaning both places. It does not refer to the two hinges.

phrases.english: MISHNA: We may restore the lower hinge pin in the Temple,
phrases.notes: This refers to the door of a carriage, box, or cupboard.

phrases.english: but not in the rest of the country.
And the upper one is forbidden here and there (in both places).
phrases.notes: It counts as real building, a Torah prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַחְזִירִין צִיר הַתַּחְתּוֹן בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the earlier discussion of the hat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lower pin: permitted in the מקדש, forbidden in the מדינה. Upper pin: forbidden in both places.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's more lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits the upper pin in the מקדש and the lower pin even in the מדינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the upper one may be restored in the Temple, and the lower one even in the rest of the country.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion. He is more lenient in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, each pin drops one level in strictness. He treats the upper pin as only a rabbinic problem, so it is allowed in the מקדש. He treats the lower pin as no problem at all, so it is allowed everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper (pin)
Lower (pin)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The upper one may be restored in the Temple,
and the lower one even in the rest of the country.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting opinion to the ruling of the תנא קמא in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upper pin: permitted in the מקדש. Lower pin: permitted even in the מדינה.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains the hinge rules and the reason behind them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא clarifies the rules. In the מדינה one may only push the lower pin back in. The upper pin is forbidden as a גזירה, in case one hammers it in. Hammering it in makes one liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the hinge pin of the door of a carriage, box, or cupboard may be restored in the Temple. In the country, one may only push it in. The upper one may not be restored in either place, as a decree lest he bang it in. And if he did bang it in, he is liable for a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains the משנה in more detail. It adds two new pieces of information.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, even in the מדינה there is a small leniency: if the pin is still partly in place, one may push it back (דוחקין). Second, the upper pin is forbidden because of a decree: one might come to hammer it in, and hammering it in is real building that makes one liable for a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught": introduces a ברייתא
One may push it back in (only when it has not fully come out)
A decree made in case one comes to do something
He will bang or hammer it in firmly
Liable to bring a sin-offering, which shows a Torah-level violation

steps.confusionAlert: "דוחקין" is not the same as "מחזירין." Pushing back a pin that is only partly out is allowed even in the מדינה. Fully reinserting the lower pin is allowed only in the מקדש.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
The hinge pin of the door of a carriage, box, or cupboard:
in the Temple, we restore it;
in the country, we may only push it in.
phrases.notes: This applies only when the pin has not fully come out.

phrases.english: And the upper one, here and there, he may not restore,
as a decree lest he bang it in.
And if he banged it in, he is liable for a sin-offering.
phrases.notes: Banging it in counts as building.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and expands the ruling of the תנא קמא from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lower pin: restored in the מקדש, only pushed in within the מדינה. Upper pin: forbidden everywhere, as a decree against hammering, which carries a חטאת.

steps.title: Doors attached to the ground may never have their pins restored
steps.stepSummary: For the door of a pit, cistern, or building extension, one may not restore the pin at all. Doing so makes one liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hinge pin of the door of a pit, a cistern, or a building extension may not be restored. And if he restored it, he is liable for a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a stricter case: doors that are attached to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier leniencies apply only to movable objects like a box or cupboard. Fixing anything attached to the ground is full building under the תורה. So it is forbidden even in the מקדש, and one who does it is liable for a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit dug in the ground
A cistern
An extension built onto a building

steps.whatToRemember: Movable object, lower pin: a rabbinic decree only, so permitted in the מקדש. Movable object, upper pin: forbidden everywhere because of the hammering concern. Attached to the ground: real building, forbidden everywhere, with a חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל בּוֹר וְשֶׁל דּוּת וְשֶׁל יָצִיעַ —
phrases.english: That of a pit, of a cistern, or of an extension:
he may not restore it,
and if he restored it, he is liable for a sin-offering.
phrases.notes: The door is attached to the ground, so this is building.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל בּוֹר וְשֶׁל דּוּת וְשֶׁל יָצִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter case to the ברייתא of step 9: doors attached to the ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Restoring the pin of a door attached to the ground is building and carries a חטאת.

steps.title: New משנה: putting a bandage back on a wound
steps.stepSummary: A bandage that came off may be put back in the מקדש but not in the מדינה. Putting one on for the first time is forbidden in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may return a bandage in the Temple, but not in the rest of the country. If it is the first time, it is forbidden here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It applies the same Temple-versus-country idea to a bandage on a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting back a bandage that slipped off is forbidden only as a rabbinic decree, in case one smears the ointment, which would be the forbidden act of smoothing. That decree does not apply in the מקדש. Putting on a bandage for the first time counts as healing, so it is not allowed even in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage or plaster with ointment
At the start, putting it on for the first time

phrases.english: MISHNA: We may return a bandage in the Temple,
but not in the rest of the country.
If it is for the first time, it is forbidden here and there.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַחְזִירִין רְטִיָּה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that follows the same pattern as the hinge pin משנה in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning a bandage: permitted in the מקדש, forbidden in the מדינה. Putting one on for the first time: forbidden in both places.

steps.title: ברייתא: a detached bandage may be returned on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. The תנא קמא rules that a bandage that came off a wound may be put back on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: A bandage that came off a wound may be put back on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה's case of a bandage by quoting a ברייתא. Its first opinion, the תנא קמא, is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows putting the bandage back, with no conditions. This is the lenient side. רבי יהודה will argue in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
A bandage or plaster spread with ointment
Came off, separated
We may put it back

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
A bandage that came off from on top of a wound —
we may put it back on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רְטִיָּה שֶׁפֵּרְשָׁה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the bandage case from the משנה (step 11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a bandage that came off may be put back on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only push it back and clean around the wound
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows pushing a slipped bandage back into place. He also allows lifting part of it to clean the wound, one side at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If it slid down, push it up. If it slid up, push it down. You may lift part of the bandage and wipe the opening of the wound. Then lift another part of the bandage and wipe the opening of the wound there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the תנא קמא. He lists only small adjustments that are allowed while the bandage is still partly on the wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only allows moves where the bandage never fully leaves the wound. That means he forbids putting back a bandage that came off completely, because it would look like bandaging the wound for the first time. Lifting one part at a time keeps the bandage on the wound.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped or slid
He pushes it
Uncovers part of it
Wipes or cleans

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get fooled by the long list of things רבי יהודה allows. He is actually the STRICTER opinion. He allows only adjustments. A bandage that came off fully may not be put back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it slipped downward — he pushes it upward,
if upward — he pushes it downward,
and he may uncover part of the bandage
and wipe the opening of the wound,
and then again uncover another part of the bandage
and wipe the opening of the wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הוּחְלְקָה לְמַטָּה — דּוֹחֲקָהּ לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה allows only pushing a slipped bandage back and partly uncovering it to clean the wound. A bandage that fully came off may not be put back.

steps.title: No wiping the bandage itself, because it spreads the ointment
steps.stepSummary: The bandage itself may not be wiped, because that spreads the ointment (ממרח). If someone spread it, he is liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he may not wipe the bandage itself, because he would be spreading the ointment. If he did spread it, he is liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to the cleaning it just allowed. You may clean the wound, but not the bandage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wiping the bandage smooths out the ointment on it. Spreading (ממרח) is a form of the מלאכה of smoothing (ממחק). That is a real Torah prohibition, so doing it brings a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreads (ointment) smooth, a form of the מלאכה of smoothing
Sin-offering brought for an accidental Torah-level שבת violation

phrases.english: But the bandage itself he may not wipe,
because he would be spreading (the ointment).
And if he spread it — he is liable for a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְטִיָּה עַצְמָהּ לֹא יְקַנֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the cleaning allowed in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wiping the bandage itself is forbidden because of ממרח. Doing it brings a חטאת.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the final ruling in the argument from the ברייתא. The ruling goes with the stricter side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, a bandage that came off completely may not be put back. Only small adjustments are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (this opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the background for מר בר רב אשי's question below.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from steps 12 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so a fully detached bandage may not be put back.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the dispute is only when it fell on a utensil
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the argument. It applies only when the bandage fell onto a כלי. If it fell on the ground, everyone forbids putting it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They only taught this when it came off onto a utensil. But if it came off onto the ground, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the case of the ברייתא. Now we know when the תנא קמא's leniency applies and when it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a כלי, the bandage is still clean and ready, so putting it back looks like continuing the old bandaging. Once it falls on the ground, putting it back looks like bandaging from scratch. So even the תנא קמא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
A utensil or object
The ground
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only
where it came off onto a utensil,
but if it came off onto the ground —
everyone agrees it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁפֵּירְשָׁה עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits where the argument in the ברייתא applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only when the bandage fell onto a כלי. On the ground, everyone forbids putting it back.

steps.title: רב אשי put back a bandage that fell on a pillow
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי tells that his father's bandage fell onto a pillow on שבת, and his father put it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: I was standing in front of my father. His bandage fell onto a pillow, and he put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רב אשי acted. It sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pillow counts as a כלי, so this is exactly the case the two opinions argue about. Putting it back looks like the תנא קמא's lenient view, which seems to go against שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing
Onto a pillow or cushion
Puts back

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
I was standing before Father,
his (bandage) fell onto a pillow,
and he was putting it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case that tests the rulings of רב חסדא and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי put back a bandage that fell onto a pillow on שבת.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי asks how his father could do this
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי asks his father: combine רב חסדא and שמואל, and a bandage that fell on a כלי may not be put back. So how could you put it back?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Doesn't the Master hold what רב חסדא said? The argument is when it came off onto a utensil, but onto the ground it is forbidden. And שמואל said the הלכה is like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The son challenges what his father did by putting two rulings together. His father answers in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says the argument is about a bandage on a כלי. שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, the stricter side. So on a כלי, like the pillow, it should be forbidden. That seems to clash with רב אשי's action.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the Master hold (this view)?
The argument applies to (this case)

phrases.english: I said to him:
Doesn't the Master hold
that which Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is where it came off onto a utensil,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פֵּירְשָׁה עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: but if it came off onto the ground — it is forbidden,
and Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action told in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's putting back a bandage that fell onto a pillow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא says the argument is about a bandage on a כלי. שמואל rules like the stricter רבי יהודה. Together they mean a bandage that fell on a כלי may not be put back, which contradicts what רב אשי did.

steps.title: רב אשי does not accept רב חסדא's limitation
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells his son he does not hold like רב חסדא's limit. Without that limit, his son's combined argument falls apart, so putting back the bandage that fell onto the pillow was allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I never heard that teaching. In other words, I do not agree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers his son's question from Step 18. He explains that he does not follow רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question only worked if you combined רב חסדא's limit with שמואל's ruling. By rejecting רב חסדא, רב אשי breaks that combination. In his view the case of a bandage that fell onto a כלי is not decided the way his son assumed, so putting the bandage back was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it (here it is a polite way of saying 'I don't accept it')
that is to say; in other words
I do not hold this view

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי rejects רב חסדא's limit. In practice he put back a bandage that fell onto a pillow on שבת, which shows that in his view a bandage that fell may be put back.
steps.confusionAlert: 'I did not hear it' does not mean רב אשי never knew about רב חסדא's teaching. The word כלומר tells us he means 'I disagree with it.'

phrases.english: He said to me: I did not hear this,
phrases.notes: The son, מר בר רב אשי, is the one telling the story.

phrases.english: meaning, I do not hold of it.
phrases.notes: He rejects רב חסדא's limitation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, כְּלוֹמַר לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question his son raised in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting one of the assumptions behind the question (רב חסדא's limitation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Combining רב חסדא with שמואל, a bandage that fell onto a כלי may not be put back.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אשי does not follow רב חסדא's limitation, so the combined reasoning that forbade his action falls away, and the bandage may be put back.

steps.title: New משנה: tying a harp string in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a string that came loose from a harp may be tied in the מקדש on שבת, but not outside it. Tying a string on for the first time is forbidden in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may tie a harp string in the Temple, but not in the rest of the country. And if it is the first time it is being tied on, it is forbidden in both places.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a rule about fixing a harp string on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying a knot is normally a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. In the מקדש the harp is used for the לויים' music at the קרבנות, so the משנה allows repairing a string that came loose there. Putting on a brand-new string is a bigger act, so even the מקדש does not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: we may tie (a real knot)
a string (of a harp)
the Temple
the rest of the country, outside the Temple
for the first time; from the start

phrases.english: MISHNAH: We may tie a string in the Temple,
phrases.notes: A harp string that came loose, used for the Temple music.

phrases.english: but not in the rest of the country.
phrases.notes: Outside the Temple there is no Temple service to justify it.

phrases.english: And if it is the first time,
phrases.notes: Tying the string onto the harp for the first time.

phrases.english: here and there it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Both in the Temple and outside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ קוֹשְׁרִין נִימָא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, another case of what the מקדש allows on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A string that came loose may be tied in the מקדש on שבת but not elsewhere. Tying a string on for the first time is forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: A ברייתא says only a bow is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says a broken harp string was not knotted, only tied in a bow. This seems to contradict the משנה, which allows a knot in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: A harp string that broke, one would not tie it in a knot, only in a bow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the harp in the מקדש, and it allows only a bow, which is not a real knot. The משנה allows a real knot in the מקדש. The two sources clash.

keyTerms.meaning: and they contrasted them (the גמרא points out a contradiction between sources)
harp; lyre
it broke; it snapped
he ties it in a bow (a loose tie, not a real knot)

steps.confusionAlert: קושר and עונב are different. A קשר is a real knot, which is a מלאכה. An עניבה is a bow, which is not a forbidden knot. The whole contradiction depends on this difference.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they contrasted it:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is bringing a source that seems to say the opposite.

phrases.english: A harp string that broke,
phrases.notes: The harp of the Temple music.

phrases.english: he would not tie it in a knot, only in a bow!
phrases.notes: This implies a knot is forbidden even in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to tie a real knot in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the same harp allows only a bow, so a knot must be forbidden even in the מקדש.

steps.title: The two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן and the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one follows the Rabbis, and that one follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each source to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources really do disagree, but they are not a problem because they come from different opinions. The ברייתא, which allows only a bow, follows the רבנן. The משנה, which allows a knot, follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult
this one... and that one
the Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
phrases.notes: Introduces the answer.

phrases.english: this follows the Rabbis, and that follows רבי אליעזר.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, and the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבָּנַן וְהָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא state the same rule and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different views: the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, the ברייתא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר allows a knot and the Rabbis only a bow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that preparations for a מצוה override שבת, so a knot is allowed for the Temple music. The רבנן hold they do not override שבת, so only a bow is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, who says that the preparations for a מצוה override שבת, he ties it in a knot. According to the Rabbis, who say they do not override, he ties it in a bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind its answer. It shows which general debate the two sources depend on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing the harp is not the מצוה itself. It is a preparation that makes the Temple music possible. רבי אליעזר holds such preparations override שבת, so a real knot is allowed. The רבנן disagree, so only a bow, which is not a forbidden knot, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: preparations that make a מצוה possible
they override שבת
he ties it in a knot

steps.whatToRemember: Tying a broken harp string in the מקדש depends on the מחלוקת over מכשירי מצוה. רבי אליעזר says they override שבת, so a knot is allowed. The רבנן say they do not, so only a bow is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects a narrow case about a harp string to a central rule found across ש״ס: whether מכשירי מצוה override שבת.

phrases.english: According to רבי אליעזר, who says

phrases.aramaic: מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, קוֹשְׁרָהּ.
phrases.english: preparations for a מצוה override Shabbat, he ties it in a knot.
phrases.notes: Fixing the harp prepares for the Temple music.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, who say they do not override, he ties it in a bow.
phrases.notes: A bow is not a forbidden knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמַר מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the answer in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the underlying principle of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is not yet clear why רבי אליעזר and the רבנן would disagree about a harp string.
steps.terutzMaskana: The disagreement depends on whether מכשירי מצוה override שבת.

steps.title: If the משנה followed רבי אליעזר, even first-time tying would be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the previous answer. רבי אליעזר's view would permit even tying a string on for the first time, but the משנה forbids that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, then even tying a string on for the first time should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own earlier answer, which said the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that preparations for a מצוה override שבת. By that logic, putting a brand-new string on the harp for the Temple music should also be allowed. But the משנה clearly forbids first-time tying, so it cannot be following רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If
From the start; here, tying a string on for the first time
Also, too

steps.confusionAlert: In this step, לכתחילה does not mean 'ideally.' It means 'for the first time' — a string that never broke and is being put on fresh.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: Refers to the previous answer, which said the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: then even tying it on for the first time should also be allowed!
phrases.notes: But the משנה forbids first-time tying in both places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִילָּה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from steps 22-23 that linked the משנה to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's rule (preparations for a מצוה override שבת) would also permit first-time tying, but the משנה forbids it. So his view does not fit the משנה.

steps.title: New answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the ברייתא follows the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the רבי אליעזר answer. It says the משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this one (the משנה) is רבי יהודה, and that one (the ברייתא) is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its old answer with a new way to explain why the משנה and the ברייתא disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a bow counts as a real tie, so there is no difference between the two. Since a bow gains nothing, the משנה allows a regular knot for a string that broke in the מקדש. The רבנן hold a bow is not forbidden by Torah law, so the ברייתא allows only a bow, which is the gentler option.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
It is not difficult — there is no real contradiction
This one… and that one — matching each source to a different opinion
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the contradiction comes from a disagreement about whether a bow counts as tying. It is not about whether a מצוה overrides שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The word אלא tells us the גמרא is dropping its earlier answer.

phrases.english: this one (the Mishnah) follows Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds that a bow equals a knot, so a knot gains nothing extra.

phrases.english: and that one (the Baraita) follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The Rabbis hold a bow is not forbidden by Torah law, so only a bow is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 24 by giving a new split of opinions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (רבי יהודה vs. the רבנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה followed רבי אליעזר, who lets מצוה preparations override שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who treats a bow as a full tie. The ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold a bow is not forbidden by Torah law.

steps.title: Whose view is רבי יהודה following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which broader opinion רבי יהודה is following. Is it רבי אליעזר's or the רבנן's view on מצוה preparations?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה — whose opinion is he following?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next move. It wants to know how רבי יהודה's view fits with the earlier argument about preparations for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a bow equals a knot for רבי יהודה, he still allows a forbidden tie on שבת. So we need to know if he agrees with רבי אליעזר that מצוה preparations override שבת, or with the רבנן who say they do not. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose view is he following?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda —
according to whose opinion (is he ruling)?
phrases.notes: Is it רבי אליעזר's view on מצוה preparations, or the Rabbis' view?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks more closely at the new answer from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר or the רבנן on whether מצוה preparations override שבת.
